opened.anchor: Ted C. Hinckley Papers, 1830-1987 - Archives West
opened.information:
**Biographical facts about Ted C. Hinckley**  
- Born “in New York City in 1925”【page_text】.  
- Educated in Pasadena, CA; BA from Claremont McKenna College, graduating in its first four‑year class in 1950【page_text】.  
- Married Scripps student Caryl Chesmore【page_text】.  
- Later earned a BS from Northwest Missouri State University【page_text】 and an MA from the University of Missouri at Kansas City【page_text】.  
- PhD in History from Indiana University, 1961【page_text】.  
- Served with the United States Navy’s Torpedo Squadron 6 during World War II【page_text】.  
- Taught history at San Jose State University for thirty‑one years【page_text】.  
- Conducted teaching assignments in Europe, Latin America, Alaska, Micronesia and was a Fulbright lecturer at the University of Gadjah Mada in Yogyakarta, Indonesia【page_text】.  
- Retired to Lake Whatcom near Bellingham, WA; continued shipboard history teaching with the U.S. Navy’s PACE program【page_text】.  
- Among his publications are diverse anthologies and three scholarly volumes on America’s nineteenth‑century Alaskan frontier, plus scripts, screenplays, and a children’s book【page_text】.  

**Collection details (Ted C. Hinckley Papers, 1830‑1987)**  
- Collection title: “Ted C. Hinckley Papers, 1830‑1987” (inclusive)【page_text】.  
- Held by Western Washington University, Center for Pacific Northwest Studies, Goltz‑Murray Archives Building, Bellingham, WA【page_text】.  
- Collection size: 30.5 linear feet【page_text】.  
- Donated by Ted C. Hinckley in 1999【page_text】.  
- Includes research and reference materials used by Hinckley, some original manuscripts, many duplicate copies and transcriptions of primary sources【page_text】.  

**Bibliographic Reference in the Collection**
